This example generates one dataset in long format, converts it to wide format,
and fits AIPW and TMLE, each with and without cross-fitting, plus pooled-targeting TMLE (TMLE-P). All analyses use logistic regression for treatment,
proportional-probit regression for the ordinal outcomes, and analytic variance
correction. The figures show time-specific point estimates and corrected 95%
pointwise confidence intervals by default, alongside a Monte Carlo approximation to the population
true value.

## Load the functions

Install the package with `R CMD INSTALL .` from the package root,
then knit this document from `vignettes/`. The example uses the installed
`DynamicDOOR` package; no source files need to be loaded manually.
See `?fit_dynamic_door` for arguments and inference options.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = TRUE,
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5,
  dpi = 144
)
```

```{r load-functions}
library(DynamicDOOR)
```

## Generate one simulated dataset

The existing `gen_toy_data()` function generates 5,000 independent subjects,
each observed at six visits. Its `$long_data` component contains one row per
subject and visit, with `id`, `time`, `Treatment`, baseline covariates `X1`--`X5`,
and observed outcome `Y`.
Outcomes have four ordered categories, with larger values representing more
desirable outcomes. The same dataset is used for all five fits.

```{r simulate-long}
long_data <- gen_toy_data(n = 5000, K = 4, seed = 0)$long_data
head(long_data)
```

### Convert to wide format

`fit_dynamic_door()` takes one row per subject and one outcome column per visit.
Specify the subject, visit, outcome, and baseline column names in `long_to_wide()`.
Treatment and baseline covariates must be constant within each subject. `times`
and `outcome_columns` specify the visit order and corresponding output names;
the outcome factor levels are preserved.

```{r convert-to-wide}
times <- c(5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30)
outcome_columns <- paste0("PrimaryDOOROutcome_collapsed_", times)
predictors <- c("X1", "X2", "X3", "X4", "X5")

obs_data <- long_to_wide(
  long_data,
  id = "id",
  time = "time",
  outcome = "Y",
  baseline_columns = c(predictors, "Treatment"),
  times = times,
  outcome_columns = outcome_columns
)
head(obs_data)
```

### Calculate the population reference values

The existing `true_psi_p_gen()` function averages the known generating category
probabilities over a separate large sample of covariates, then calculates the
population win probability at each visit. With `M = 100000`, this gives a Monte
Carlo approximation to the true values. The five fitted analyses still use only
the single dataset of 5,000 subjects generated above.

```{r population-truth}
true_values <- true_psi_p_gen(M = 100000, K = 4, seed = 123)
truth <- data.frame(time = times, true_psi = true_values$true_psi)
```

## Fit the five methods

The arguments below explicitly identify the treatment, outcomes, predictors,
category order, and visit times. We use `scale = FALSE` to match the original
simulations: binary covariates are already coded 0/1, and continuous covariates
are generated with SD 1 and moderate means. In practice, `scale = TRUE`
standardizes all numeric predictors to sample mean zero and SD one before fitting.

Explicitly supply `outcome`, `varc`, and `correction`. Here `varc = TRUE` with
`correction = "proposition"` computes both ordinary EIF-based and parametrically
corrected inference. All three cross-fitted analyses use the same seed and
five-fold partition. The time average assigns equal weight to each visit.

We request `ci_trajectory = "both"` so the same fit can display pointwise or
chi-square simultaneous bounds without refitting. Set `plot = FALSE` during
fitting because the following chunks draw each plot explicitly. `plot = TRUE`
would display and store the plot when the fit is created.

```{r common-arguments}
common_arguments <- list(
  obs_data = obs_data,
  treatment = "Treatment",
  outcome_columns = outcome_columns,
  trt_predictors = predictors,
  outcome_predictors = predictors,
  outcome_levels = as.character(1:4),
  times = times,
  outcome = "polr",
  varc = TRUE,
  correction = "proposition",
  ci_trajectory = "both",
  plot = FALSE,
  V = 5,
  seed = 1,
  scale = FALSE,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  weights = rep(1 / length(times), length(times))
)
```

Each call to `plot()` uses the existing `plot.dynamic_door()` method.
Colored points are estimates and error bars are corrected 95% confidence
intervals. The black dotted curve is the population truth approximated above;
the gray dashed reference line is 0.5. To display ordinary EIF-based intervals
instead, set `corrected = FALSE`.

```{r plot-reference}
truth_layer <- ggplot2::geom_line(
  data = truth,
  mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = time, y = true_psi),
  inherit.aes = FALSE,
  color = "black",
  linetype = "dotted",
  linewidth = 0.9
)
```

### AIPW without cross-fitting

```{r fit-aipw}
fit_aipw <- do.call(
  fit_dynamic_door,
  c(common_arguments, list(method = "AIPW", cf = FALSE))
)
```

```{r plot-aipw}
plot(fit_aipw, corrected = TRUE, ci_trajectory = "pointwise", xlab = "Time (days)") +
  truth_layer +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "AIPW without cross-fitting",
    subtitle = "Black dotted line: population truth (Monte Carlo)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = "#2563A6") +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none")
```

### AIPW with cross-fitting

```{r fit-aipw-cf}
fit_aipw_cf <- do.call(
  fit_dynamic_door,
  c(common_arguments, list(method = "AIPW", cf = TRUE))
)
```

```{r plot-aipw-cf}
plot(fit_aipw_cf, corrected = TRUE, ci_trajectory = "pointwise", xlab = "Time (days)") +
  truth_layer +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "AIPW with five-fold cross-fitting",
    subtitle = "Black dotted line: population truth (Monte Carlo)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = "#16817A") +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none")
```

### TMLE without cross-fitting

```{r fit-tmle}
fit_tmle <- do.call(
  fit_dynamic_door,
  c(common_arguments, list(method = "TMLE", cf = FALSE))
)
```

```{r plot-tmle}
plot(fit_tmle, corrected = TRUE, ci_trajectory = "pointwise", xlab = "Time (days)") +
  truth_layer +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "TMLE without cross-fitting",
    subtitle = "Black dotted line: population truth (Monte Carlo)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = "#A86B16") +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none")
```

### TMLE with cross-fitting

```{r fit-tmle-cf}
fit_tmle_cf <- do.call(
  fit_dynamic_door,
  c(common_arguments, list(method = "TMLE", cf = TRUE))
)
```

```{r plot-tmle-cf}
plot(fit_tmle_cf, corrected = TRUE, ci_trajectory = "pointwise", xlab = "Time (days)") +
  truth_layer +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "TMLE with five-fold cross-fitting",
    subtitle = "Black dotted line: population truth (Monte Carlo)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = "#8052A4") +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none")
```

### TMLE with pooled targeting

TMLE-P uses the same held-out nuisance predictions as TMLE-CF, but estimates a
shared fluctuation across evaluation folds.

```{r fit-tmle-p}
fit_tmle_p <- do.call(
  fit_dynamic_door,
  c(common_arguments, list(method = "TMLE-P", cf = TRUE))
)
```

```{r plot-tmle-p}
plot(fit_tmle_p, corrected = TRUE, ci_trajectory = "pointwise", xlab = "Time (days)") +
  truth_layer +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "TMLE with pooled targeting",
    subtitle = "Black dotted line: population truth (Monte Carlo)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = "#B84D58") +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Compare pointwise and simultaneous inference

`ci_trajectory` accepts `"pointwise"`, `"simul"`, or `"both"`. For $T$ visits,
pointwise bounds use $z_{1-\alpha/2}$ and simultaneous bounds use
$\sqrt{\chi^2_{T,1-\alpha}}$ times the visit-specific SE. The latter are coordinate
projections of a joint Wald ellipsoid. The time-average interval remains pointwise.

Reuse the AIPW fit to display both types of bounds with ordinary and corrected
inference. Dark bars show pointwise intervals; light bars show the projections
of the chi-square joint region.

```{r plot-ci-comparison, fig.width=8}
plot(fit_aipw, corrected = TRUE, ci_trajectory = "both", xlab = "Time (days)") +
  truth_layer + ggplot2::labs(title = "AIPW: corrected inference")
```

Joint membership uses the full covariance matrix $\widehat V$ of the estimated
trajectory:

\[
(\widehat{\boldsymbol\psi}-\boldsymbol\psi_0)^\top
\widehat V^{-1}(\widehat{\boldsymbol\psi}-\boldsymbol\psi_0)
\leq \chi^2_{T,0.95}.
\]

`joint_tests` evaluates the supplied `null_trajectory`, which defaults to 0.5 at
every visit. Checking whether all plotted bounds contain a trajectory is not the
same as this joint test. Singular covariance makes joint inference unavailable;
the code does not substitute Bonferroni intervals.

```{r joint-inference}
knitr::kable(fit_aipw$joint_tests, digits = 4)

# Evaluate the Monte Carlo population reference using the corrected covariance.
region <- fit_aipw$joint$corrected
difference <- fit_aipw$fit$psi - truth$true_psi
statistic <- as.numeric(crossprod(difference, region$precision %*% difference))
data.frame(statistic = statistic, critical = region$critical,
           reference_in_region = statistic <= region$critical)
```

## Compare the time-averaged results

The plots display individual visits. This table reports the equally weighted
time average, its ordinary and corrected standard errors, and its corrected
95% confidence interval. Complete visit-level results remain available in
`results` and in each fitted object's `$results` component.

```{r collect-results}
fits <- list(
  "AIPW" = fit_aipw,
  "AIPW with cross-fitting" = fit_aipw_cf,
  "TMLE" = fit_tmle,
  "TMLE with cross-fitting" = fit_tmle_cf,
  "TMLE-P" = fit_tmle_p
)

result_tables <- vector("list", length(fits))
for (i in seq_along(fits)) {
  result_tables[[i]] <- data.frame(
    method = names(fits)[i],
    fits[[i]]$results,
    row.names = NULL
  )
}
results <- do.call(rbind, result_tables)
```

```{r average-results}
average_results <- results[results$target == "average", c(
  "method", "estimate", "se", "se_corrected",
  "ci_lower_corrected", "ci_upper_corrected"
)]

knitr::kable(
  average_results,
  row.names = FALSE,
  digits = 4,
  col.names = c(
    "Method", "Estimate", "EIF SE", "Corrected SE",
    "Corrected CI lower", "Corrected CI upper"
  )
)
```
